newsitem.title: USA: MobileMedia Corp eyes default, debt sinks.
newsitem.headline: MobileMedia Corp eyes default, debt sinks.

text.p: MobileMedia Corp's 9-3/8 percent notes sank more than 10 points in early trade on Monday after the company said it may not be able to make interest payments, high-yield traders said.
The notes were quoted at 65 bid, 70 offer at mid-morning, according to high-yield analysts and traders. The company's zero coupon bonds slipped to 55.
MobileMedia said expected third-quarter earnings would place it in violation of certain loan covenants and it is now deciding whether to make November coupon payments.
The company said it has begun talks with agent banks on the matter. The banks could prevent an $11 million interest payment on the notes, sources said.

Les Levi, high-yield media and telecommunications analyst at Merrill Lynch & Co Inc, said the announcement reopened the wound sustained late last month when the company first said third-quarter earnings would place it in violation of bank covenants. MobileMedia debt fell sharply and then stabilized in recent weeks, Levi noted.

"Today's announcement was that they were mulling a decision as to whether they were going to make the payment on the coupon, or whether the banks would allow them to; that's really what scared the market," Levi said.
Levi said the company normally would have a 30-day grace period before a technical default is declared. Further, he said the company does have the cash to complete the payments.
"We've seen companies like this go into the grace period and make the payment before the period ends to avoid defaulting," he said.

Moody's Investors Service on Monday lowered MobileMedia's senior subordinated note rating to Caa from B3 following the announcement. Standard & Poor's cut MobileMedia notes to CCC from B-minus in August.
